items.briefing:
Australian organisations are seeing a sharp rise in email fraud where attackers are exploiting trusted credentials — meaning criminals are using legitimate-looking email accounts or login details to trick staff into taking action. This type of attack is particularly hard to spot because the emails appear to come from real, known sources. Staff should be especially cautious about unexpected requests involving payments, login links, or sensitive information, even if the sender looks familiar.

**Practical tip:** If you receive an unexpected email requesting urgent action — even from a known contact — verify it by calling the sender directly before responding or clicking anything.

featured.title: Attackers exploit trusted credentials in email fraud surge
featured.quote: Email fraud now accounts for 45% of incidents as attackers bypass multi-factor authentication defences.
